comment: Galena is lead ore, and raw galena dusted onto a pot and fired with it in one pass is exactly how lead-glazed earthenware was made from about 1400 BCE. No new item, no glaze bucket, no second firing. The nugget rather than crushed galena on purpose: the crushed form exists in vanilla but adds a pointless step. Cassiterite is tin ore and goes on over a lead base, because that is what tin glaze is — a lead glaze opacified with tin oxide, invented in 9th-century Baghdad to imitate Chinese porcelain. It costs both nuggets, and the tin layer is what your food touches, so tin-glazed ware does not poison you.
